newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close lower tracking U.S markets.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close lower tracking U.S markets.

text.p: Argentine bonds plunged Wednesday following a 1.93 percent decline in the Dow Jones .DJI and the spike in the U.S. long bond yield back towards seven percent, dealers said.
"The fall was foreseeable as the market, after having risen strongly in the past few days, had no strength to bear the decline in the U.S. markets," a broker said.
Argentina's dollar-denominated FRB due 2005 ended 7/8 lower at $92.35/92.50 while Bocon Previsional 4 shed $0.78 to close at $114.85/115.00.
"The market is still dependent on the U.S. figures, although investors have already discounted a possible U.S. rates hike by the Fed," an analyst said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve meets May 20 to set its monetary policy.
Analysts advise to take profits at these levels and maintain current portfolios.
